notes.title: Update b0.B
notes.content:
- Added stage six
 == This stage has some variance between playable characters. Try them all!
- About 25 new items
- New achievements associated with stage six and new items
- Two more of the fourth stage boss' patterns have been overhauled, including their final
 == Overall, they should both be easier-to-understand and more consistent to dodge
- Massive, global performance improvements
 == Bullet functionality was entirely reimplemented in C++
 == Native-language functionality was also given substantial discernment
 == More performance improvements still to come in the future to allocate for our upcoming wasteful deluges
- Many item balance changes
 == Most notable buff goes to Kiai, which goes from "never been used" to "impossible to not use"
 == Most notable nerf goes to Armor-piercing Runes. Don't worry, it's still really good
- New curses, reworked curses, and new wards
 == The max curse value is presently +82. We advertised +88 on Bluesky a bit ago, but one of those had to be cut at the last minute for stability reasons. Might bring it up to +88 in a hotfix
 == Needless to say. I would not recommend playing +82 for the general playerbase
- Reworked fumos
 == Lives are now tied to the fumo and will be lost if the fumo is sold
 == The  will only devalue once its associated life has been lost
 == Additionally, all fumos now provide a small stat up
- Overall more consistent, faster, and synergetic item behavior

This is the final major update before 1.0.
Next time, you will see everything.
Savor the questions you have right now, because you can't go back once you learn.
I eagerly await our final meeting.

notes.title: Update b0.A - QoL and Polish
notes.content:
Currently, we're working on a couple engine changes that should massively improve the game's performance, and are holding off on releasing stage six until those are done. It's sooooo cool though. I play it and its like "woah. this is the future" and I showed it to the other kids at lunch break and one dude said he would trade me a shiny Tepig for a copy but I know it's worth at least a Victini.
However, due to the large time gap between the early access release and the time it looks like that stuff is going to be done, I've decided to bring a lot of the recent additions to the live versions of the game.

For the early access copies, this means:
- Improved vfx overall, particularly for enemy and boss destruction
- Visual shop transitions
- Bookmarks that let you pause and resume runs partway through
 = These are automatically created in the event of crashes (most of the time)
 = These are WIP and imperfect but I figured would be more helpful than not to include
- Achievement tracker, unlocked after defeating the stage 5 boss for the first time
- A couple new items scattered in the mix
- Some reworked and rebalanced items
- Some reworked patterns, most notably on the stage 4 boss
- Changed the way active items determine what slot they use
 = You now select the slot of an item by pressing the correlated button to buy it
 = The setting for changing the default sorting method was removed, but I am thinking about bringing it back in the future depending on how this feels
- You can now control the player with the mouse through a setting
 = This is also imperfect and not fully-compatible with a few items such as Occultist's Fit but I thought it would be neat since a few people have expressed interest in this sort of control scheme

For the demo, this includes the above changes in addition to ones to make it more closely represent the early access release, such as:
- Updated art
- Reworked Sumireko
- Substantially more pattern changes
- Generally making the game more fair

stage six coming when it's done, but hopefully everything's ready before next touhoufest!

notes.title: Approaching Steam Demo
notes.content:
Patch notes:

Additions:
- Sumireko Usami! Not all of her graphics are complete
- Rebind menu for keyboard and controller!
- Proper controller support!
- Some of the sound effects. Not all of 'em yet
- Character profiles and spell/non practice menu
- Music room
- A little pop-in tells you the name of the track that's currently playing
- Reisen gets a new spellcard
- Effect for dying and respawning
- Knockback on hit
- A lot of menus
- Some new items with WIP items
- A better tutorial!
- Spell capturing via graze
- Achievements with unlocks

Changes:
- Lasers are temporarily removed
- Stages available reduced to two from four. The other four exist, but it's a vertical slice-type deal
- Item get notifications work better
- Shop positions within a constellation are consistent
- Magic circle rooms now only care about graze, which determines how much health you get at the end
- Reimu, Chiyuri, and Yumemi all have new sprites that better reflect their design in this game
- A level of bomb charge stat now increases the amount charged per room by a whole tick instead of half
- Shot power cap is no longer determined by your current shot type
- All the boss patterns in the game have been polished and better tuned for each difficulty
- Decided to use capitalization in patch notes for some reason
- Grazebox clears bullets while invincible
- Spell charge stat now also increases the deathbomb window
- Large amount of miscellaneous balance changes
- All the menus that were there are better

Overhauls:
- Map system removed!
 = We noticed it was causing a lot of confusion with new players, and despite many attempts to articulate it well in tutorials I never found any way to do it well. This game has a lot of new mechanics and the map system ended up being extremely taxing to both players and for development.
- There are only three stats now!
 = Shot power, spellcard charge, and grazebox. The orbitals and collection stats have been removed so as to streamline the game in coordination with the removal of the map system. Item prices have been adjusted across the board to reflect this.
- No more JavaScript!
 = Ultimately it ended up not being as performant as we were hoping, and was again causing a huge strain on development.
- The game is a single route now!
 = Huh!? Well, we thought about some things and decided it wasn't feasible for us to put all three routes in a single game, and it would be cooler to split them up into three games. Each one will have a self-contained story, with some leadins to the others. So long as we are financially able to keep developing, we can make two more games that not only sport the rest of the story, but more mechanics such as the reintroduction of the map system, and, eventually, modding support.
- Challenge system!
 = And now for the good side of major changes, the challenge system. Customize your run with curse-like effects or see how well you fare without certain mechanics for a higher score and special unlocks.
- Achievements and score system! It's not in yet, but I promise it'll be cool!
 = Score is now exclusively based on how many achievements you get in a run. This involves common things such as defeating bosses, as well as difficult or special things like collecting fumos, getting a certain amount of graze, or having challenges on.

Fixes:
- Deathbombing used to crash? On god?
- Pause-related bugs
- Window-related issues
- Chiyuri's default shots are cool again
- No more map-related issues, I think
- Visual inconsistencies with shot types
- Score indicator wasn't getting reset properly
- A huge amount of other things, you wouldn't even believe it, oh my god

Bada bing.
If you're concerned that we are about to push this with minor changes to steam public, don't be.
There's a couple major things that'll make it feel like a real one.
